# Generated by iptables-save v1.8.13
# The SSH throttle was written as "-m limit -j ACCEPT" with no --limit: the
# match falls back to 3/hour, burst 5, and iptables-save prints it that way.
# The first five new connections of a test get in; after that, one every 20
# minutes. The drop log has the same default and goes quiet after five
# lines. The HTTPS throttle states its rate and is fine.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -s 10.0.0.0/8 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m limit --limit 3/hour -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m limit --limit 50/sec --limit-burst 100 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m limit --limit 3/hour --limit-burst 10 -j LOG --log-prefix "FW-INPUT-DROP: "
COMMIT
